assessments.reasoning: All three captures refer to gcc-mirror/gcc commit 04696df09633baf97cdbbdd6e9929b9d472161d3 and the same config.sub SHA-256 as the claim. Their ranges [0,16384), [16384,32768) and [32768,35295) cover the entire file. The first contains the copyright, base grant, inclusion clause, section 7 sentence and GNU Config upstream locator. The remaining text supplies no conflicting grant.

The pinned License Index scope document admits additional permissions as exceptions and requires evidence for instrument boundaries, authority and edition before merging identities. That rule applies to the extra section 7 sentence. The publisher specimen supplies the wording and the index owns the classification.

challenge.method: I tested a merge with elisp-comp and an attribution to Autoconf’s own generated output. I checked the file’s GNU Config identification, GCC distribution path, object of the grant, and final sentence in the exception paragraph.
challenge.results: The script identifies itself as GNU config.sub and points to GNU Config upstream. Its permission concerns including “this file” with a program containing an Autoconf-generated configuration script. Of the two publisher specimens inspected, only config.sub expressly designates the permission under GPLv3 section 7.

limitations: The finding covers the FSF-copyrighted GNU Config file in the pinned GCC tree. The 2021-10-27 timestamp belongs to the script. Other GCC or GNU Config files and editions require their own evidence.
The file’s conditional grant is separate from Autoconf’s standalone Configure Script Exception. Active carries no finding about current project-wide licensing.
reasoning: GNU Config’s config.sub, as distributed in the named GCC specimen, follows the conditional file-inclusion grant with “This Exception is an additional permission under section 7 of the GNU General Public License, version 3 (\"GPLv3\").” That sentence identifies the distinct documentary form. Active is its editorial registry mapping.
